title: Contact Injury

positions.as_written: Ask where the blow landed: the outside of the knee, the inside, the front, or the lower leg.
Ask which way the knee bent or was pushed as a result.
Ask whether the foot was planted at the time, because a planted foot converts a blow into a much larger joint force.
Ask whether they could weight bear immediately and whether the knee swelled, and how fast.
Ask about the knee feeling like it came apart or went out and back in, which raises a dislocation.
Any high energy contact injury should prompt assessment for a combined injury rather than a single structure, which is the main difference from the non-contact mechanism.
